history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Padri-Ki-Haveli ('Mansion of the Padre'), formally the church of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, is the oldest church in Bihar and a Roman Catholic cathedral under the Diocese of Patna. Roman Catholics built the first small church here in 1713 (Capuchin monks); Nawab Mir Qasim's soldiers destroyed it on 25 June 1763 during his quarrel with British traders, burning its ancient records. The present structure was redesigned by the Venetian architect Tirreto of Kolkata in 1772 (foundation 70 ft x 40 ft x 50 ft) and was damaged again during the 1857 rebellion. Its landmarks include the large Ashtadhatu 'Maria' bell gifted in 1782 by Bahadur Shah, son of Nepal's King Prithvi Narayan Shah. Mother Teresa stayed here for three months in 1948 for nurse training before beginning her mission; her room is preserved. The church celebrated its 300th anniversary in 2013. One official source says the Jesuits built it while others say Capuchins (conflict flagged).

name: Padri Ki Haveli
town_description: Patna, the capital of Bihar on the southern bank of the Ganges, is among the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities - the ancient Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan and Gupta empires. Padri Ki Haveli stands at Sonar Toli, Gurhatta in Patna City (old Patna), the eastern historic quarter of the city. Patna today is a major administrative, educational and religious centre with a 2011 population of about 1.7 million.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna, approx. 7-8 km; taxis and app cabs available.
travel.railway: Patna City station nearby; Patna Junction approx. 5 km west; auto-rickshaws serve the Gurhatta area.
travel.road: Sonar Toli, Gurhatta, Patna City area; reachable by auto-rickshaw, taxi and city bus through the old city.

visitor_information.best_time: September to April for pleasant weather. Christmas season is the most festive time to visit, with decorations and larger crowds.
